message:
Stiff load path carries survival wind to the post without damage. Plain words: the whole disc at full wind pushes like a heavy shopping bag, and a short steel post clamp takes that push as a small twist at its base. I take from the Pennsylvania State University Wind Energy Club CWC Technical Design Report (E16) that thrust force on the blades is transmitted to the front face of the nacelle and creates a bending moment on the tower counteracted by the baseplate connection, which I use for the stiff nacelle bedplate with two-bearing shaft housing (C8); the survival thrust (E22) is 37.3 N, about 3.80 kg weight, and the overturning moment at the post clamp (E23) is 13.1 N·m, matching the turbine-gust-load-check skill (E20) range of 36.1 N to 45.1 N.

Deflection and stress leave large margins. Plain words: the post bends less than a millimetre, so the spinning blades cannot be pushed into the tower or the cube walls. I take from the Collegiate Wind Challenge 2023 - University of Colorado - Design Report (E18) that competition tower practice is 1.5 inch outer diameter, 1/8 inch thick 6061 aluminium tubing, which I use for the post; the post tip deflection (E26) is 0.516 mm against 25.0 mm side clearance, and the bending stress (E27) is 16.6 megapascals (MPa) against 240 MPa yield for 6061-T6 aluminium from the thin-wall-aluminium-frame-sizing skill (E21), a factor of about 14.

Envelope keeps rotating parts inside the box with rub margin. Plain words: a 40 cm spinning disc centred in a 45 cm box leaves a finger width each side, and tilting the shaft up plus hanging the rotor upwind keeps that gap open when it bends. I take from the Turbine Design Report - 2024 Collegiate Wind Competition - California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo (E19) that nacelle plates and mounts are made from 6061 aluminum, which I use for the bedplate; the side-view layout with rotor clearance and post interface (E28) shows rotor plus nacelle inside the cube with only the post below outside, and the tilt plus overhang clearance concept (C9) keeps the 2.50 cm per-side gap positive under the 0.516 mm deflection (E26).

Not ready, because Manager selection between hub, nacelle and clearance concepts plus interface to brake rails still needs decision.
